text:
maria: Heads-up — production hosted-api started returning 502/504s ~09:12 UTC during the cert rotation + model swap. Customers report streaming disconnects and a bunch of client-side retries. Ticket #CS-8321 opened.
chris: Can you paste a sample request + trace id? any throttles showing?
maria: sample curl from customer: `curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwv1-large","input":"hi"}'`
maria: Response we saw: `HTTP/2 502` with body `{"error":"upstream error","code":502}`. Trace header the client provided: `x-rd-trace: rd:7f2a9d3b`.
sre-bot: Alert: edge-gateway-502s spike detected (rate: 18/min) across eu1/us1. Matching pattern: upstream connect errors during TLS handshake.
kai: Noted. We just flipped certs on frontdoor at 09:10 and rolled model rwv1-large -> rwv1-quant at 09:11 in hosted pool eu1. Could be a midproxy TLS mismatch or jostled keepalive.
chris: Maria — can you run `kubectl logs -n infra ingress-edge-xxxxx | grep "rd:7f2a9d3b" -A10 -B5` and paste the envoy upstream error lines? Also check `nginx` error logs on the same pod.
maria: Pasted excerpt: ```
[2025-02-08T09:12:14Z] envoy upstream connect failure, reason: TLS handshake, peer: 10.23.45.12:443, downstream_remote: 34.56.78.90
[2025-02-08T09:12:14Z] route: /v1/generate, request_id: rd:7f2a9d3b, upstream_host: midproxy-eu1-2
[2025-02-08T09:12:14Z] connection closed while waiting for response
```
maria: nginx error log: `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream` repeated ~180x over 3m.
kai: That looks like midproxy ejection during cert swap — likely ALPN/HTTP2 reset between frontdoor and midproxy. I can temporarily pin the route to the fallback model on eu2 and divert traffic away from the midproxy pool.
chris: For quick mitigation: 1) route customer traffic to eu2 fallback (no model swap) 2) increase upstream-timeout on frontdoor from 60s -> 90s 3) disable in-flight cert reloading on failing revision. Can ops run 1 & 2 now?
maria: Running shelter route: `rb route update --route hostedapi --region eu1 --dest eu2-fallback --reason "502 spike"` — switching now.
sre-bot: Action taken: route update submitted by maria at 09:18 UTC. Watch for error rate drop.
maria: Error rate fell from 18/min -> 3/min in 2m after reroute. Some customers still see single 502 during reconnects.
chris: Next: grab pcap of frontdoor<->midproxy for 09:09-09:15 window, and check for TLS renegotiation failures. Also pull midproxy pod events: `kubectl get events -n hosted --field-selector involvedObject.name=midproxy-eu1-2`
maria: Events show `BackoffStart` and `Liveness probe failed` during same minute — pod restarted once. Logs show `failed to load cert revision rev-2025-02-08-0910: transient IO error`.
kai: That matches a failing cert hot-reload causing connection resets. We'll stop the rolling cert job for now and pin to previous revision. Eng-runtime, can you look at the hot-reload path? If the loader returns EIO it can tear active connections.
chris: I'll open an eng-runtime ticket and include these logs + trace header. Maria, add a short reproducer for SRE playbook: 1) trigger cert flip on frontdoor 2) concurrently swap model in hosted pool 3) observe 502 pattern with `rd:*` traces. Put curl + headers + min repro script in the ticket.
maria: Done — attached `repro.sh` to the ticket and included `kubectl` outputs. Customer notified about temporary reroute and asked for ETA.
chris: Short-term ETA: 2h to fully roll back cert automation and validate reload path. Long-term: add graceful reload that drains upstream connections before replacing cert handles. Also add a fallback to accept previous cert while new one warms.
kai: Agreed. Also suggest adding a healthcheck that verifies TLS handshake with midproxy before marking cert revision as ready.
sre-bot: Incident update: reduced severity to P2 after successful reroute and pod stabilization.
ticket-bot: CS-8321 updated: mitigation applied, eng-runtime assigned, customer notified.
maria: Thanks — leaving this thread open while eng-runtime digs in. If anyone sees recurring 502s after 10:00 UTC re-escalate immediately. :wave:
